draft.title: Economic growth and GDP
card: Gross domestic product is the value of all final goods and services made in a country in a year.
Economic growth is GDP rising over time. It is usually shown as a percentage change from one year to the next.
GDP measured after removing the effect of price rises. Growth is measured with real GDP, so it shows more being made, not just higher prices.

Only final goods and services count, those sold to their end user. GDP counts what is made inside the country, whoever owns the business. It includes services such as haircuts as well as goods such as cars.
draft.remember: Growth means real GDP rising: more goods and services made, not just higher prices.

a.q: Which statement best describes economic growth in a country?
opts: More goods and services being made in the country
More people being born or moving into the country
Higher average prices for goods and services sold
More businesses opening up in the country
a.why: Economic growth is real GDP rising, which means more final goods and services are made. Higher prices alone do not count, because real GDP removes the effect of price rises.
a.clue: Think about what real GDP measures once price rises are removed.

b.q: Real GDP in a country was $900 billion in one year. The next year it was $936 billion. What does this show?
b.why: Real GDP rose from $900 billion to $936 billion, so more goods and services were made and the economy grew. Real GDP has the effect of price rises removed, so it cannot show that prices rose, and it says nothing about jobs.
b.clue: Real figures have already had price rises taken out.

a.best: More goods and services being made in the country
